He mocked the chairman
now every seat in the house
no dam holds a laugh

Chalk dust on my sleeve —
a machine cracks the problem
I pour it a drink

like a flushed-out main.

stops paying rent to a ghost —
I own my own pipes

The ledger goes blank
where their names were crimes; I watch
the ink let them go

A ship on her side
the whole manifest counted
not a miracle

the neighbors get to speak now.
A seam, not a wall.

water will run uphill soon—
a pope says it won't

Machines that must drink
deeper than the town's old well —
one neighbor said no

Ballots fill the main
the old mains still carry hope

River keeps its course
votes outrun the chainsaw's roar
I let out my breath

Rails did what rails do
until this morning in Spain—
thirty empty seats

water keeps its say

a pipe clears, one man walks home

and the flow stays whole

ballots gather like good rain
the old pipes still hold

sixty-two years to the sea
I raise my old glass

no untested water flows

a valve the White House shut tight

pressure finds its ease

a valve cracked, and time flows on

still we dig for the living
a thousand names lost

dissent's cold water runs clear,
students drink again.

and swallowed a sleeping town

could ever carry

off the terror list, at last
old pipes, new water

swings open again

one American walks free

the blockage clears, he walks out
water finds its way

I've seen this valve stuck
seventy years sealed—Seoul asks
let the current flow

a judge shut the backflow off

Old eyes, borrowed glass
millions still, the moon slides through

shelved before the concrete dries—
still, I mix more sand

to narrowing their own valve

a young life dammed at the shore

old pipes, older hearts.

Crews cut a firebreak
as heat leans on Bordeaux vines
I know that thirst well

Twenty years, same town
the fever met its old drain
and stayed underground

turns, the old minister steps
down, current flows on

the street clears its throat

a moving van at Downing,

a billion of us
packed around one patch of grass —
the good kind of war

to watch walls give up

as if hunger ever once

smiles rowed up like clean fenceposts

a word I trust like weather

born here is born here. full stop.
some days we're still us

five days under stone
and the street still claps for one —

all our satellites, and still
hope travels by hand

good. let them. dance on

eleven thousand
hands that move the world's breakfast

first, and bare-handed

clean water, my old trade, still
the best diplomat

a ring of fire round the dark—

one by one the capsule climbs,

where no nation ends

bounced across the rusted sand,

strangers climbed the wall and hugged,
a city breathed whole

no heaven, no hell, just us,
the world holds its breath

a cartoon too long to work,
the whole world believed

between two star-crowded plates—

the rest, he said, is our job
